correctness.rationale: The occurrence-start residues of any factor form a cyclic indicator subset, and differences between equal-size windows reduce exactly to oscillation across circular arcs. Every arc oscillation is at most min(t,p-t) <= floor(p/2). Attaining equality forces the support to be a single circular block of size floor(p/2) or ceil(p/2); for p>=4 two adjacent starts force a constant-letter pattern. The run-length comparison then gives the iff criterion. Small periods 2,3 are handled explicitly. A separately implemented checker tested 974 binary primitive and 3222 ternary primitive periods; finite tests only corroborate the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Optimal uniform factor-balancedness is a natural intrinsic invariant of a word, quantifying every possible pattern and comparison window. The theorem gives a sharp p-only bound for every primitive period, a complete all-alphabet structural classification of equality by largest/second-largest cyclic run lengths, and explicit extremizers for each period. This is not an arbitrary parameter slice or finite table and provides a structural calibrated benchmark for recent quantitative factor-balance research.
